({{g|Scarlet and Violet}}: [[The Teal Mask]]) |colors=yes |eyes=Red |hair=Yellow }} {{Character Infobox/Game |color={{scarlet color light}} |gen={{gen|IX}} |games={{pkmn|Scarlet and Violet|Scarlet, Violet}} }} {{Character Infobox/Anime |color={{scarlet color light}} |series=''[[Pokémon Horizons: The Series]]'' |debut=''[[HZ071|Encounters at the Crystal Pool]]'' |enva=[[Samia Mounts]] |jpva=[[Yū Shimamura]] }} |} '''Briar''' (Japanese: '''ブライア''' ''Briar'') is a character introduced in [[The Teal Mask]] in {{g|Scarlet and Violet}}. She is a teacher at [[Blueberry Academy]], the descendant of historian [[Heath]], and also the one in possession of the original [[Scarlet Book]]{{sup/9|S}}/[[Violet Book]]{{sup/9|V}}. ==In the core series games== Briar first appears after the Treasure Hunt main story starts. The player learns that Briar is a descendant of [[Heath]], the author of the [[Scarlet Book]]{{sup/9|S}}/[[Violet Book]]{{sup/9|V}}. She owns the original copy of the book, which contains unredacted information on the Pokémon {{p|Terapagos}}.'''Briar''': ''"[...] I even have his original manuscript. Look here—these are the pages that were blacked out and made illegible in the published version of the book. The Pokémon depicted on these pages is called {{p|Terapagos}}. [...]"'' ({{g|Scarlet and Violet}}: [[The Teal Mask]]) As Heath was discredited for his writings in the book, Briar seeks to find Terapagos to prove Heath's theories correct. While waiting for her request to enter [[Area Zero]] to be approved, she leads the {{player}} and several other students on a class trip to [[Kitakami]]. During [[The Teal Mask]] story, Briar does research on the land while [[Carmine]], [[Kieran]], the player, and other students explore Kitakami. Briar appears at [[Crystal Pool]] after the player and Carmine defeats a {{p|Milotic}}. She explains that the crystals found in Kitakami emit energy similar to [[Terastal energy]] found in [[Paldea]]. Briar believes she can find a way to use the [[Terastal phenomenon]] usable outside of Paldea, bringing her closer to finding Terapagos. After the player defeats Carmine at Loyalty Plaza, Briar calls Carmine and the player to meet up in the community center. Briar reveals that she, Carmine, and Kieran are returning to [[Blueberry Academy]] earlier due to a development at the [[Great Crater of Paldea]]. Due to this, the trip to Kitakami ends earlier. Between the end of The Teal Mask and [[The Indigo Disk]], Briar has traveled to many different regions with Carmine assisting her. Eventually, she was able to create a special "Terarium Core" that hung on the top of the [[Terarium]], allowing Terstalization to occur in Blueberry Academy. Briar returns in [[The Indigo Disk]] after the player defeats Kieran. She later was permitted by [[Geeta]] to finally start a new expedition to Area Zero alongside the player, [[Kieran]], and [[Carmine]]. During the trip, she discovers the [[Area Zero Underdepths]] and the 19th Tera Type, {{type|Stellar}}. After reaching the deepest part of the Area Zero Underdepths, she and Kieran awaken Terapagos. After Kieran captures Terapagos, she encourages him and the player to fight to see Terapagos's true power. After Kieran loses, Briar suggests he Terastallize Terapagos to see its full power. Upon seeing Terapagos Stellar Form, she declares this is the Hidden treasure of Area Zero. However, this causes Terapagos to lose control and cause havoc. She then watches the player, Carmine, and Kieran defeat Terapagos, resulting in the player's capturing of it. She then apologized for her reckless behavior and obsession. After returning to Blueberry Academy, she writes a [[Briar's Book|book]] containing the information she learned from Area Zero. Upon talking to the player in Classroom 1-4, she apologizes and reveals that the player, Carmine, and Kieran's [[Tera Orb]]s have been powered up due to Terapagos, allowing them to Terastalize without the need to recharge. She then reveals that [[Snacksworth|a man in a blue suit]] was waiting to meet the player at the academy's entrance. Arrangement |- style="background:#FFF" ! rowspan="1" |{{GameIcon|Sc}}{{GameIcon|Vi}} | When talking to Briar | Briar* | Unknown | Unknown |- | class="roundybottom" style="background: #{{violet color}}; color:#fff;" colspan="5" | '''Song names marked with an asterisk are unofficial, as they have not received a soundtrack release.''' |} ==In animation== [[File:Briar anime.png|250px|thumb|Briar in {{aniseries|HZ}}]] ===''Pokémon Horizons: The Series''=== ====History==== At some point in the past, Briar, alongside [[Carmine]], encountered a {{p|Terapagos}} capable of achieving its {{type|Stellar}} form. This encounter led to Briar becoming a expert for this species of Pokémon. Briar was first mentioned in ''[[HZ068|Into a New Sky! The Brave Olivine!]]'', [[Raifort]] indicated that [[Liko]], [[Roy]], and [[Dot]] needed to meet her because of their current research on {{p|Terapagos}}. In ''[[HZ069|Roy is Crocalor, and Crocalor is Roy!]]'', it was revealed by her student, Carmine, that Briar was at the [[Crystal Pool]]. In ''[[HZ071|Encounters at the Crystal Pool]]'', Briar met [[Friede]], Liko, Roy and Dot at the Crystal Pool, she immediately wanted to study {{an|Terapagos}} upon seeing it, and with the group she soon discussed information on Terapagos, its forms, and [[Area Zero]]. Briar additionally started talking about her ancestor [[Heath]]'s discoveries and research regarding Area Zero, which she intended to prove to be true despite them having been publicly dismissed as fiction. When Friede asked her information on [[Laquium]], Briar had not heard of it before, but was nonetheless interested in finding out more about it. In ''[[HZ078|Entei's Fierce Battle Cry!]]'', Briar contacted the [[Rising Volt Tacklers]], informing them of the sighting of {{p|Gouging Fire|a Pokémon resembling Entei}} made within Area Zero and asking them to meet her back at [[Paldea]]. In ''[[HZ080|Total-lie Awesome Pokémon in Area Zero?!]]'', Briar met up with the Rising Volt Tacklers and showed them around Area Zero, before settling down for camp she informs Liko, Roy and Dot about the calls Scream Tail makes. In ''[[HZ081|The Pillar of Fire]]'', Briar witnessed the battle between the Rising Volt Tacklers and Lucius's "Entei". Upon witnessing its unusual appearance, its use of {{m|Burning Bulwark}}, resistance to Water-type moves and further research into the [[Scarlet Book]], she realized that Lucius's "Entei" was really a Gouging Fire. After the Rising Volt Tacklers pass Gouging Fire's test, Briar witnessed Gouging Fire showing off its memories and how it met Lucius, before going back into its Ancient Poké Ball. In ''[[HZ082|Beyond the Shining Rainbow]]'', Briar witnessed Liko and the Rising Volt Tacklers' battle against Rayquaza. Initially, she was taking care of Terapagos, but when Liko's Tera Pokémon entered the battle, Briar witnessed the Pokémon's enormous power. At the end of the battle, Briar said goodbye to the group and said that everything she witnessed will help her in her personal research for [[Briar's Book|her book]]. Briar reappeared in a flashback in ''[[HZ085|The Pokémon Paradise of Laqua!]]''. A year later, in ''[[HZ108|Taking the Next Steps]]'', Briar was contacted by Liko to answer some questions, however Briar revealed that with the increasingly tight deadline for the delivery of her book, she was unable to respond at that moment and promised to contact Liko in the future. [[File:Briar and Pagogo.png|250px|left|thumb|Briar and [[Pagogo]]]] Some time later, in ''[[HZ111|Better, Farther, Stronger!]]'', Briar returned Liko's call and revealed that she had completed her book, with the free time, she invited Liko and the other Rising Volt Tacklers to visit the [[Blueberry Academy]]. In ''[[HZ115|Welcome to Blueberry Academy!]]'', Briar spoke with Liko and her friends via [[Rotom Phone]], revealing that she couldn't meet with them because she was helping with maintenance on the Blueberry Academy's Terrarium. [[HZ116|The following day]], Briar and Carmine gathered Liko, Roy, Dot, and [[Ult]] to begin her studies at the [[Strong Sphere]], [[Laquium]], and especially {{TP|Liko|Terapagos}}. In ''[[HZ117|Ult-imate Training]]'', Briar contacted the Rising Volt Tacklers and [[Penny]] again to inquire about Pagogo's eating habits and personal details. During the meeting, Liko helped Briar with her research, much to Carmine's displeasure. In ''[[HZ119|Don't Give Up, Crocalor!]]'', Briar reunited the group to present the partial results of her research. Using [[Diana]]'s and [[Jacq]]'s research and her own personal experience, Briar theorized that the Rising Volt Tacklers would need to gather all [[Type|eighteen existing]] [[Terastal phenomenon|Tera-type]]s for Pagogo to be able to use his full power and thus end the Laquium existing on the planet. According to her, these eighteen types must come from Pokémon with strength comparable to that of the [[Six Heroes]]. After Roy's battle against [[Drayton]], Briar bid farewell to Pagogo and the Rising Volt Tacklers, asking to be updated on anything they might discover in the future. ====Character==== [[File:Briar book anime.png|250px|thumb|Briar and [[Briar's Book|her book]] about Terapagos]] Briar has a kind and jovial attitude, being friendly and kind to those she meets. Briar has a big sense of curiosity, getting easily excited to things related to her ancestor's research amonst other things, such as encountering Terapagos, and wanting to learn more about Area Zero's history and such. In ''[[HZ071|Encounters at the Crystal Pool]]'', Briar revealed that she is writing a book telling her discoveries about the real history involving Area Zero, because of this, she has not yet found her ideal [[first partner Pokémon]]. ====Pokémon==== Briar has no Pokémon. artwork | ''{{color2|000|Pokémon Horizons: The Series}}'' concept art |} =====Eyecatch===== {| style="margin:auto; text-align:center; {{roundy|5px}} border:2px solid #{{violet color dark}}; background:#{{scarlet color}}; font-size:80%" |style="{{roundy|5px}} border: 2px solid #{{violet color dark}}; background: #{{scarlet color light}}; width:auto"| [[File:HZ eyecatch Briar.png|x150px]] |- |} ==In the TCG== [[File:BriarStellarCrown163.jpg|200px|thumb|Ultra rare print of Briar]] {{main|Briar (Stellar Crown 132)}} '''Briar''' is introduced as a {{TCG|Supporter card}} in the [[Pokémon Trading Card Game]] during the English Scarlet & Violet Series (the Japanese Scarlet & Violet Era). It was first released in the Japanese {{TCG|Stellar Miracle}} expansion and the English {{TCG|Stellar Crown}} expansion, with artwork by [[Naoki Saito]]. An {{TCG|ultra rare}} version with artwork by the same illustrator and a {{TCG|special illustration rare}} version of the card illustrated by [[DOM]] were released in the same sets. This card can only be used if the opponent has exactly 2 Prize cards remaining. It allows the player to take 1 more Prize card if their opponent's Active Pokémon is Knocked Out by damage from an attack used by the player's {{DL|Pokémon ex (TCG)|Tera Pokémon ex|Tera Pokémon}}. {{-}} ==Trivia== * Briar's earrings resemble the [[Terastal phenomenon]]'s six-pointed star logo, her jacket and pants are colored like the [[Violet Book]] and the [[Scarlet Book]] respectively, and her jacket is also decorated with the same patterns as the Scarlet Book (on her left) and the Violet Book (on her right). * Briar's [[Rotom Phone]] uses a [[List of clothing in Pokémon Scarlet and Violet#Rotom Phone|Scarlet Case]]{{sup/9|S}}/[[List of clothing in Pokémon Scarlet and Violet#Rotom Phone|Violet Case]]{{sup/9|V}}. * In {{aniseries|HZ}}, Briar mentions that she's already encountered a {{p|Terapagos}}, which seems to be a reference to the {{ga|Terapagos|one}} she met during the events of [[The Indigo Disk]]. ** Additionally, she mentions that she's writing a book, which seems to be a reference to the [[Briar's Book|one]] she writes after the events of The Indigo Disk. ==Names== {| class="roundtable" style="background:#{{Violet color}}; border:3px solid #{{Violet color dark}}" |- ! style="background:#{{scarlet color light}}" | Language ! style="background:#{{scarlet color light}}" | Name ! style="background:#{{scarlet color light}}" | Origin |- | Japanese | ブライア ''Briar'' | From ''{{wp|briar}}'' (common name for a few species of thorny plants; {{wp|Erica arborea|tree heath}}) |- | English, Indonesian | Briar | From ''briar'' |- | German | Brianna | From ''briar'' |- | European Spanish,
